reply.line: Good evening, gentle ones. Sister Vesper, of the Drowned Choir. The hour is struck, the water is still, and I would ask you to hum along. Any note will do.
A little, when the river lets me. The notes come out a few seconds late and rather damp. That is the sound of it. Hum with me, and we will be late together.
The hour is vespers, as it has been since the chapel went under. It is always vespers, somewhere. I keep it so that no one else has to.
Nothing so frightening. A hymn for the lost, in three parts: one for the water, one for the bell, and one for whoever is listening. That part is yours.
Hum, if you can. Not loudly, and not in tune. The river is fond of a ragged chorus, and it has had, I think, rather a lot of them.
The bell sounds under the surface. You will not hear it unless you are quiet, and then you will hear nothing else. Shall we try?
